sentence_stem: The phone was off all evening, so
correct_completion: he must have forgotten to charge it.
full_sentence: The phone was off all evening, so he must have forgotten to charge it.
acceptable_variants: he must have left it at home.
he might have run out of battery.

options.text: he will be late for work.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' expresses a future prediction, but the stem describes a past situation that needs a past explanation.

options.text: he must have forgotten to charge it.

options.why_wrong: 'Would have called' describes an imagined past result, not a logical conclusion about why the phone was off.

options.text: he can go to school tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This talks about a future possibility and gives no reason for the phone being off in the past.

grammar_focus: Modal perfect 'must have + past participle' for a logical deduction about the past
explanation: 'Must have' plus a past participle expresses a confident conclusion about a past situation, based on evidence. Polish speakers often use a simple past verb here, because Polish does not have a separate modal perfect structure.
translation: Telefon był wyłączony przez cały wieczór, więc on musiał zapomnieć go naładować.
